title: FlexiCache: Leveraging Temporal Stability of Attention Heads for Efficient KV Cache Management
one_line: A vLLM fork that classifies KV heads as temporally stable or unstable, keeps full KV on the GPU only for unstable heads while offloading stable heads' non-top-K pages to pinned host memory, and periodically re-ranks stable heads to fetch back newly promoted pages.

repo.evidence: Paper §1 final contribution bullet and Artifact Appendix A.3.1 both give https://github.com/NazmulTakbir/FlexiCache; the GitHub account matches first author Nazmul Takbir (ntakbir@uci.edu, paper p.1). repo/README.md:6 states 'Accepted to MLSys 2026' and repo/FlexiCache/README.md:77 gives the Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18918856 also printed in the paper's Appendix A.2. The repo contains the full system (vllm/v1/flexicache/, vllm/attention/ops/flexi_cache_triton_kernels.py, 4 CUDA kernels, modified allocator/scheduler), not a placeholder.
repo.badge_evidence: none found - the MLSys 2026 proceedings page (https://proceedings.mlsys.org/paper_files/paper/2026/hash/94bcb01789fccf15afe2764d8fe0f40e-Abstract-Conference.html) was fetched and lists no badges and no code link. The repo does ship FlexiCache/Artifact_Evaluation.pdf and a Zenodo DOI (10.5281/zenodo.18918856), which evidences an AE submission but not an awarded badge.

H1_open_repo.evidence: Official (see repo.evidence) and substantive: vllm/v1/flexicache/{config.py,model_data.py,config.json} + 4 hand-written CUDA kernels under vllm/v1/flexicache/kernels/cuda/ (kv_d2h_tx_gpu_mapped.cu, h2d_copy_blocks.cu, topk_swap_map.cu, block_table_h2d_dirty.cu), ~1200 lines of sparse-decode and MinMax-scoring Triton in vllm/attention/ops/flexi_cache_triton_kernels.py, hierarchical allocation in vllm/v1/core/{kv_cache_utils.py:643-704,kv_cache_manager.py,block_pool.py:29-49}, reload/pause scheduling in vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:115-122,172-175,601-603,716-727, plus complete eval scripts (FlexiCache/{LongBench.sh,Throughput.sh,LEval.sh}, benchmarks/FlexiCache/**).

H2_no_root.evidence: Install is conda + 'pip install -e .' (FlexiCache/README.md:85-110); no kernel module, eBPF, perf counters, KVM, /proc/sys or hugepage step anywhere in the FlexiCache path. The 24 sudo and 147 docker red-flag hits in repo_facts.json are all in upstream vLLM Dockerfiles and docs/source/** that the artifact instructions never invoke. Host pinning uses torch pin_memory (vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:2002) and cudaHostRegister (vllm/v1/flexicache/kernels/cuda/kv_d2h_tx_gpu_mapped.cu:218), both driver-mediated, not root-gated. Only external binary is optional numactl at benchmarks/FlexiCache/Throughput/Llama8b.sh:90, which its own comment (:84-88) says is a no-op on single-socket hosts.

H3_hardware_fit.evidence: Single-GPU by construction (every script passes --tensor-parallel-size 1; that is the entire multi_gpu grep hit set). The artifact asks for 80 GB HBM minimum, >=256 GB host RAM, a 180 GB pinned pool and PCIe Gen5 (FlexiCache/README.md:32-35; paper §4.1) vs our 24 GB / 125 GB / PCIe 4.0, but every capacity knob is exposed data: cpu_kv_cache_size and avg_num_tokens_per_req in vllm/v1/flexicache/config.json, --max-model-len/--max-num-seqs/--topK-budget on the CLI, with pool sizing derived in vllm/v1/flexicache/config.py:148-193 and vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py:643-704. Scale-down arithmetic: Llama-3.1-8B fp16 (16.1 GB weights) with --max-model-len 8192 makes the per-layer GPU-block floor fall back to ceil(8192/16)*8 = 4096 blocks/layer ~= 1.1 GB (config.py:186-188), inside the ~3.5-4.5 GB of KV budget left on 24 GB; at 6-8k-token prompts FlexiCache needs ~1408 GPU blocks/layer/request vs 4096 for dense, so it still roughly doubles the batch and genuinely exercises hierarchical placement, stability-aware rerank and sparse decode. All four CUDA kernels are arch-generic (uint4 copies, atomicAdd, __threadfence_system, cudaHostRegister) and compile for sm_86 by changing TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST as README.md:167 instructs. Residual concern (documented, not a fail): config.py:190-193 aborts hard if the floor is unmet, and PCIe 4.0 halves the bandwidth §3.3's overlap argument assumes, so the speedup ratio may shrink even if the system runs.

H4_obtainable_deps_data.evidence: All deps are user-space PyPI/conda (requirements/cuda.txt:8-11 torch==2.6.0; flexicache_requirements.txt transformers==4.50.0, datasets<4, huggingface_hub<1; artifact A.3.3 Triton 3.2.0, Python 3.12); no system package is required, and CUDA 12.4 nvcc installs into a conda env. Data: LongBench via load_dataset('zai-org/LongBench') (benchmarks/FlexiCache/Language_Modelling/LongBench/run_benchmark.py:61-63), L-Eval harness vendored at benchmarks/FlexiCache/Language_Modelling/L-Eval/LEval/ (MIT), throughput workload bundled in-repo at benchmarks/FlexiCache/Throughput/Prompts/prompts-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct.json, and head profiles hardcoded in vllm/v1/flexicache/model_data.py. No proprietary traces. Two frictions, neither blocking: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 (config/model2path.json) need a free click-through HF licence (artifact A.2), and flexicache_requirements.txt:4 'fastchat' is almost certainly a typo for 'fschat' (PyPI fastchat is an unrelated 0.1.0 stub) that will break run_benchmark.py:8.

reproduce.target: Paper Table 3 = artifact §A.6.1 Table 7: LongBench accuracy retention for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, avg FlexiCache/dense ratio = 1.00 at topK-budget 64 pages (1024 tokens), 64 unstable heads, rerank frequency 16 - the claim that the never-discard hierarchy preserves model quality under a 1024-token attention budget. Produced by 'bash FlexiCache/LongBench.sh Llama8b'. Stretch target: paper Figure 5(a) = artifact §A.6.2 Table 8 (token throughput vs output length, FlexiCache-1024 over vLLM, 1.11x-2.08x) via 'bash FlexiCache/Throughput.sh Llama8b'.
reproduce.scale_down: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct fp16 (fallback Mistral-7B-v0.2, 1.6 GB smaller, profile also shipped). Set --max-model-len 8192-16384 and mirror it into benchmarks/.../LongBench/config/model2maxlen.json (default is 131072, which makes the config.py:186-188 block floor demand ~17 GB). Lower vllm/v1/flexicache/config.json avg_num_tokens_per_req 20000 -> 6000-8000 and cpu_kv_cache_size 180 -> 32-48 GB (only 111 GiB host RAM free, pool is pinned). Prompts 10k-30k -> 4k-8k; --max-num-seqs 64 -> 8-16; --num-prompts 500 -> 80-150; output lengths 100/500/1000 first. TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST '9.0;9.0a' -> '8.6'. Compare the FlexiCache/dense ratio at identical truncation and batch, not absolute LongBench scores.
reproduce.effort: 5 person-days + ~20 GPU-hours (1 d env/build, 1.5 d memory-budget surgery and block-floor/pinned-pool debugging, 0.5 d harness edits, 2 d runs+analysis; ~4 GPU-h accuracy subset, ~10 GPU-h throughput sweep, ~6 GPU-h retries)
reproduce.rationale: Not H: the artifact's stated minimum is 80 GB HBM / 256 GB host RAM / PCIe Gen5 (FlexiCache/README.md:32-35), i.e. 3x our GPU memory, 2x our RAM and 2x our interconnect, so the configuration must be re-derived rather than replayed; vllm/v1/flexicache/config.py:190-193 turns an under-sized GPU budget into a hard ValueError that desk review cannot prove satisfiable; and §3.3's claim that a reload 'typically completes within one decode step' is tuned for 64 GB/s, so the throughput ratio specifically may not carry to PCIe 4.0. Not L: every script, config file, prompt corpus (bundled JSON) and head profile needed for both headline results is in the repo; the knobs that must change are plain config values and CLI flags; the four CUDA kernels are arch-generic and JIT-built for the local arch; pins (torch 2.6.0+cu124, Triton 3.2.0, transformers 4.50.0) are ~1 year old but all installable; the harness emits exactly the CSVs the appendix promises; and the artifact went through MLSys AE with a Zenodo archive and published expected numbers (FlexiCache/README.md:148-175).

addons.name: Per-head drift-triggered rerank intervals
addons.hypothesis: We hypothesize that giving each KV head its own rerank deadline, driven by its online measured top-K drift, improves LongBench/L-Eval accuracy retention at equal throughput (or throughput at equal retention) compared with FlexiCache's binary stable/unstable split plus a fixed 16-step interval, under long-context long-generation workloads.
addons.mechanism: At every rerank both the previous and the new top-K sets are already resident on the GPU (old_top_k_blocks and top_k_blocks are passed side by side into the swap-map kernel at gpu_model_runner.py:2313-2325). Add a small kernel that computes, per (layer, head), the paper's own random-corrected overlap (§2.2) between them and folds it into an EMA. Replace the scalar 'dec_step % rank_f == 0' test with a per-head deadline: re-rank a head when its predicted RCO falls below a target tau, with floor/ceiling on the interval. Deliberately leave the memory layout untouched (unstable heads still keep full KV on GPU, stable heads still keep only top-K) so the block allocator and pool-sizing math are unaffected and the change stays inside the worker. Expose tau as a CLI flag next to --rerank-frequency.
addons.motivating_evidence: Paper §2.3 verbatim: 'While stability scores of heads form a continuous spectrum, we adopt a binary classification (stable vs. unstable) for system simplicity. In principle, a finer-grained categorization (e.g., multiple stability tiers with different reranking intervals or top-K budgets) could further specialize KV management policies. However, such designs introduce additional control complexity ... By restricting the design to two classes, we keep the control-plane overhead minimal.' Figure 1 shows per-head RCO decaying at visibly different rates within one layer. Table 6 shows retention moving with the interval and unstable fraction (0.9932 -> 0.9628), and §4.5 closes with 'Further model- or workload-specific tuning could likely yield additional throughput gains.'
addons.feasibility_rationale: Localized: one new overlap kernel, a per-head deadline array, and a changed branch - well under 1k LOC across three files. All the tensors it needs (old_top_k_blocks, top_k_blocks, block_scores) already exist on the GPU at exactly the right moment, so no new data path or allocator change is required. Evaluable end-to-end with the shipped FlexiCache/LongBench.sh, LEval.sh and Throughput.sh at the §4 scale-down; clearly within reach of 2-4 students in 10 weeks.
addons.research_value_rationale: It is precisely the generalisation the authors name in §2.3 and explicitly defer on control-plane-complexity grounds, so an MLSys reviewer would want the answer. Both outcomes teach: if per-head intervals win, it is a measurable improvement over a just-published system; if the bookkeeping overhead eats the gain, that empirically validates the paper's simplicity argument, which is itself a reportable result.

scoop_check.details: Queries: 'FlexiCache arXiv 2511.00868 citing papers'; 'adaptive rerank interval sparse attention KV cache per-head budget allocation 2026'; 'online runtime head classification without offline profiling 2026'. Closest: Predict, Reuse, and Repair (https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.30389) uses an EMA predictor over top-K block selections, but to hide the selection->attention dependency entirely within GPU memory - no offloading, no memory hierarchy, no per-head interval scheduling. Ada-KV (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2407.11550) adapts per-head *budgets* for eviction, not per-head rerank *frequency* under a GPU/host hierarchy. Semantic Scholar shows no follow-up work on FlexiCache itself. Nothing found that adapts FlexiCache's rerank interval.

addons.name: Does temporal stability survive genuinely long generation?
addons.hypothesis: We hypothesize that FlexiCache's accuracy retention degrades monotonically as generation length grows from ~400 to >=4000 output tokens at a fixed 16-step rerank interval - because top-K drift accumulates over many more windows - and that a drift-triggered rerank recovers most of the loss, on LongGenBench/LongWriter-style long-form generation.
addons.mechanism: Build a generation-length-swept harness on top of the existing LongBench driver: reuse run_benchmark.py's vLLM setup but substitute LongGenBench/LongWriter prompts and max_tokens in {500, 1k, 2k, 4k, 8k}; report the FlexiCache/dense retention ratio at each length for rerank interval in {8, 16, 32} with the unstable fraction fixed at 25% (the only shipped profile). Additionally instrument per-head RCO as a function of decode-step index to see whether stability itself decays with position rather than only the top-K set. Then re-run with the drift-triggered rerank from add-on 1.
addons.motivating_evidence: The paper makes the case itself in §4.3: 'LongBench ... has a key limitation in evaluating sparse attention: most tasks generate short outputs ... the average generation length is below 50 tokens.' It therefore switches to L-Eval - but its own Table 4 shows L-Eval generations are only 81-390 tokens. So the differentiator over eviction methods, 'long-context, long-generation' (§1, §7), is never measured past ~400 tokens. §1 cites LongWriter and LongGenBench ('benchmarks evaluating LLMs on outputs as long as 32k tokens') and then never evaluates on them.
addons.feasibility_rationale: Needs a new workload driver and a new scoring metric (LongGenBench's per-task checks), which the repo does not provide; and generating 4k-8k tokens x dozens of samples x 3 interval settings x {dense, FlexiCache} is compute-heavy on one A5000. Affordable at reduced sample counts (~15-25 GPU-h) and it composes with add-on 1, but it is a new harness rather than a knob change.
addons.research_value_rationale: It tests the paper's headline claim in exactly the regime the paper claims to target and never measures. A clean negative (stability holds out to 8k output tokens) strengthens the published result; a positive (retention decays with generation length) identifies a real limitation of the fixed interval and directly motivates the adaptive design. Either way a reviewer at MLSys learns something about the paper's central premise.

scoop_check.details: Queries: 'LongGenBench OR LongWriter sparse attention KV cache accuracy long generation degradation'. SCBench (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2412.10319) and Retrospective Sparse Attention (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2508.09001) both establish that long-generation tasks are far more KV-budget-sensitive than long-input tasks - supporting evidence for the hypothesis - but neither evaluates FlexiCache, head-stability tiers, or a GPU/host hierarchy. No work found that stress-tests FlexiCache's rerank interval against generation length.

addons.name: Online head classification, dropping the offline profiling pass
addons.hypothesis: We hypothesize that the stable/unstable head partition estimated online from the serving system's own rerank-time top-K overlaps, after a short warm-up, matches the LongBench accuracy retention of FlexiCache's offline ~2 GPU-hour profile within noise, letting FlexiCache be applied to an unprofiled model with no offline pass.
addons.mechanism: Warm-up phase: run the first N requests with all heads treated as unstable (full KV on GPU, rerank every step - a configuration --num-unstable-heads already supports), accumulating per-(layer,head) RCO from old_top_k_blocks vs top_k_blocks; at the end of warm-up freeze the bottom-quartile set and apply it to subsequent requests. Compare the derived set against the shipped gov_report set in model_data.py using the paper's own Table 1 overlap metric, and compare end-to-end LongBench retention. Complication to engineer around: FlexiCacheConfig is a process-wide singleton whose head sets drive per-layer GPU/CPU pool sizing at startup, so the pools must be sized for the worst case and the partition swapped only at request boundaries.
addons.motivating_evidence: §2.3 and footnote 1 make offline profiling a per-model prerequisite (~2 h for Llama-3.1-8B on GovReport), and §4.2 stakes the design on the 'model-intrinsic' claim (mean cross-task overlap 0.76-0.83, Tables 1-2). But the artifact ships only precomputed head sets for four models in vllm/v1/flexicache/model_data.py and does NOT ship the dumper feeding TopK-Analysis: TopK-Analysis/preprocess.py:40 expects Data-Sorted/<model>/<dataset>/sample-*/decode-step-{N}-prompt-len-{P}.pt tensors that nothing under vllm/ writes. A fifth model therefore cannot be supported today, and Table 6's unstable-fraction ablation is unreachable because config.py:88-95 asserts on profile keys that only exist for M in {64,80,128}.
addons.feasibility_rationale: The measurement half is trivial (same GPU tensors as add-on 1), but swapping the partition interacts with per-layer pool sizing (config.py:148-173 feeding kv_cache_utils.py:671) and the per-(layer,head) block allocator, which is cross-cutting rather than local; worst-case pool sizing also costs GPU memory that is scarce on a 24 GB card. Still a well-scoped 10-week job for 2-4 students with the existing LongBench harness for validation.
addons.research_value_rationale: It removes the artifact's single biggest usability limitation (no new model can be profiled with what is released) and independently re-tests the paper's central claim that head instability is model-intrinsic, using a different estimator than the authors'. A disagreement between the online-derived and shipped offline head sets would be a substantive finding about §2.3.

scoop_check.details: Queries: 'online runtime head classification retrieval streaming heads without offline profiling LLM KV cache 2026'; 'papers citing FlexiCache arXiv 2511.00868'. DuoAttention (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.10819) and the HeadKV/Ada-KV family classify heads but all via an offline optimisation or profiling pass; HeadWiseKV (https://arxiv.org/html/2609.02029) does budgeted per-head cache residency, again with precomputed head roles. No work found that derives FlexiCache-style stability tiers online from a serving system's own rerank telemetry.

addons.name: Bandwidth-aware FlexiCache for commodity PCIe 4.0 / small-HBM GPUs
addons.hypothesis: We hypothesize that on a PCIe-4.0, 24 GB-HBM machine FlexiCache's fixed operating point (25% unstable heads, K=64 pages, interval 16, CHUNK_PAIRS=8192, GRID_BLOCKS=32) leaves throughput on the table, and that a start-up calibration measuring actual host-to-device block-copy bandwidth and then choosing the transfer-shaping parameters and rerank interval recovers a measurable fraction of the gap to the paper's H100/PCIe-5 speedups.
addons.mechanism: (i) A calibration pass at engine init that times the existing h2d_copy_blocks kernel over a synthetic promoted-page set across several (chunk_pairs, grid_blocks) points and picks the knee - both are currently hardcoded constants in the reload path. (ii) A cost model relating measured bandwidth, observed promoted-KV volume per rerank (Table 4 reports 44-67 MB for Llama-3.1-8B at budget 2048) and decode-step time, used to pick the rerank interval so a reload still finishes inside one decode step - the assumption §3.3 states but never checks against bandwidth. (iii) Report a bandwidth-sensitivity curve (throttling effective H2D bandwidth by varying grid_blocks) as the headline figure.
addons.motivating_evidence: §4.1 pins the testbed to 'PCIe 5.0 with a peak bidirectional bandwidth of 64 GB/s' and 180 GB of host KV cache. §3.3 asserts that reloads 'typically complete within one decode step' and that 'only a small fraction of the batch (about 1/16 for a rerank frequency of 16) is idle at any point' - both bandwidth-dependent claims. The paper contains no sensitivity study to interconnect bandwidth or HBM capacity, and the three SM-contention techniques in §3.3 (low-priority stream, capped grid, chunking) appear with fixed constants and no tuning methodology (CHUNK_PAIRS = 8192, GRID_BLOCKS = 32 hardcoded in the reload path).
addons.feasibility_rationale: The calibration harness is new code and the parameter sweeps are GPU-hour-heavy. Worse, one natural axis - the unstable-head fraction - is effectively frozen: vllm/v1/flexicache/model_data.py ships only M in {64, 80, 128} and vllm/v1/flexicache/config.py:88-95 asserts on the exact profile key, so exploring 12.5% or 6.25% (paper Table 6) requires add-on 3 or a re-written dumper first. Still fits this machine and a 10-week term.
addons.research_value_rationale: A portability/sensitivity study answering 'does this design survive on the hardware most people actually have?' is genuinely useful and directly stress-tests two unquantified assumptions in §3.3. But a reviewer would read it as careful characterisation plus parameter auto-tuning rather than a new mechanism, and hiding PCIe latency for sparse attention is already a crowded space.

scoop_check.details: Queries: 'PCIe 4.0 vs PCIe 5.0 KV cache offloading bandwidth sensitivity host-to-device stall'; 'prefetch predicted promoted KV pages hide host-to-device reload stall vLLM 2026'. STS (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.15508) prefetches KV blocks over PCIe Gen5 using speculative token sparsity; vLLM Hybrid HiSparse (https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-09-08-glm53-part1-hybrid-sparse-offloading) and tiered KV offloading (https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-09-10-tiered-kv-offloading) now ship hot/cold GPU-host tiering for sparse MLA. None calibrate to measured bandwidth or study FlexiCache's head-stability-driven reload volume specifically, but the prefetch-to-hide-PCIe idea itself is taken.

risks: 24 GB HBM is the binding constraint and the failure mode is a hard abort: vllm/v1/flexicache/config.py:190-193 raises ValueError('Not enough GPU blocks to satisfy per-layer minimum'). The floor is ceil(avg_num_tokens_per_req/block_size)*num_kv_heads*4 with a fallback to ceil(max_model_len/block_size)*num_kv_heads; with Llama-3.1's default max_model_len=131072 and the shipped avg_num_tokens_per_req=20000 neither term is satisfiable on a 24 GB card holding 16 GB of weights. Both must be lowered by hand, and LongBench/run_benchmark.py:136-149 does not currently expose max_model_len. Desk review cannot prove a satisfying point exists - test this first.

PCIe 4.0 (~32 GB/s) vs the paper's PCIe 5.0 (64 GB/s, §4.1). §3.3's overlap argument rests on a reload finishing inside one decode step; halving the bandwidth may push it past one step, so the scheduler's per-request pause (vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:172-175) stops being 'about 1/16 of the batch' and the throughput ratio shrinks. The system may work while the headline speedup does not reproduce - itself a legitimate Contemporary-track result.

Pinned-memory allocation at scale: gpu_model_runner.py:2002 allocates the entire host KV pool with pin_memory=True and then cudaHostRegisters it (kv_d2h_tx_gpu_mapped.cu:218). CUDA pinned allocations normally bypass RLIMIT_MEMLOCK, but a 32-48 GB non-swappable reservation on a shared 125 GiB machine (111 GiB free at measurement) is still large. Unverifiable by reading.

The stability observation itself is not reproducible as shipped: TopK-Analysis/ consumes Data-Sorted/<model>/<dataset>/sample-*/decode-step-*.pt files (TopK-Analysis/preprocess.py:40) that nothing in the repo produces. Figure 1 and Tables 1-2 cannot be regenerated, no new model can be profiled, and Table 6's unstable-fraction ablation is unreachable because model_data.py ships only M in {64,80,128} while config.py:88-95 asserts on the exact key.

Gated model weights: artifact A.2/A.3 require accepting the Llama-3.1 licence on Hugging Face and a logged-in account, whereas env.md only guarantees non-gated HF reachability. Free but a gate; Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 is the fallback (profile shipped, 1.6 GB smaller).

Day-one environment papercuts: flexicache_requirements.txt:4 requests 'fastchat' but run_benchmark.py:8 needs the 'fschat' distribution (PyPI fastchat is an unrelated 0.1.0 stub from 2024-02-29); benchmarks/FlexiCache/Throughput/Llama8b.sh:90 unconditionally prefixes numactl, which may not be installed; README.md:151 hardcodes Hopper arch flags '9.0;9.0a' for the runtime JIT of the four .cu files. All trivially fixed but all will bite.

CUDA 12.4/12.8 wheels on driver 535: cu124 wheels normally run on >=525 via minor-version compatibility and the FlexiCache kernels are JIT-compiled for the local arch, so this should be fine, but any JIT/PTX path assuming a newer driver is a known risk class on this machine. System nvcc is 11.8, so a conda cuda-toolkit 12.4 install is mandatory.

Model-specific kernel branch: vllm/attention/ops/flexi_cache_triton_kernels.py:949 defines kernel_compute_block_scores_minmax_qwen32 alongside the generic scorer at :818, hinting at shape-specific specialisation - a sign that supporting a fifth model may need more than a head profile.
Unmaintained artifact: repo created 2026-03-04, last pushed 2026-03-09, 3 stars, 0 open issues, no commits since. Expect no upstream support.
